name: the trace notes nothing
why: The whole feature: without _mbGateTrace() this script is absent from String Theory's Network log again.
grep: T1: a clicked cell is one request

name: the label keeps /ws/2/ and fmt=json
why: The log names a request as upstream's mbnFetch() labels it; a raw path is a different label than his scripts write for the same request.
grep: T1: a clicked cell is one request

name: every request is background in the log
why: A click is foreground (b: 0), as the gate books it; the log's lanes tell them apart.
grep: T1: a clicked cell is one request

name: the Relationships column gives no reason
why: The log's Reason column is how a reader tells the column's requests from a preview's.
grep: T1: a clicked cell is one request

name: each retry gets a new id
why: The log pairs events by id: without one id per request, a 503 and its retry show as two requests.

edits.replace:
const id = undefined;
        let gaveUp = false;

grep: T2: a 503 and its retry stay one request

name: the answer drops MusicBrainz's rate-limit headers
why: X-RateLimit-Who says whose budget ran out; the log shows it, upstream writes it.
grep: T2: a 503 and its retry stay one request

name: the answer does not say the hold it set
why: The hold a 503 set is what the log draws as a band across the lanes.
grep: T2: a 503 and its retry stay one request

name: one storage write per event
why: #1095: a write per event re-parsed the whole trace and fired a storage event in every other MusicBrainz tab each time; events wait a second and go in one write.

name: page fetches are not logged
why: A list's pages are most of this script's traffic; logged only, never paced (upstream's mbnLog()).

edits.find:
const res = await _mbGateLogFetch(url, init ? { credentials: 'same-origin', ...init } : { credentials: 'same-origin' },
                    { reason: 'pages' });
edits.replace: const res = await fetch(url, init ? { credentials: 'same-origin', ...init } : { credentials: 'same-origin' });

name: the flush replaces the tab's trace
why: Several writers share one tab's key (his copies of the gate and this one): the flush appends, never replaces.

name: idle tabs are never swept
why: Without the sweep every closed tab's trace stays in localStorage for good.

name: the trace ignores the switch
why: sa_mb_shared_gate off means this script leaves the shared schedule alone, its trace included.

name: secrets are not hidden
why: A copied log is posted in issues; a token in a URL must show as •••.
grep: T7: a secret in a URL is hidden

name: the log's icon is never written
why: Without the mbu.logIcons entry String Theory's Network log draws its own icon on this script's rows.
grep: T8: the first write names this script's icon

name: the icon write drops other scripts' icons
why: mbu.logIcons is shared: replacing the object takes every other non-member's icon out of the log.
grep: T8: the first write names this script's icon

name: the icon is written on every page
why: One read per page is the cost; a write each time touches every tab's storage event for nothing.
grep: T9: with the entry already there

name: a broken mbu.logIcons value is kept
why: An array or a string in the key would leave this script without its icon for good.
grep: T10: a broken mbu.logIcons value is replaced

name: the icon is written with the gate off
why: Off means nothing: the icon is named only where the trace runs, i.e. once there are rows.
grep: T6: switched off, no trace is written
